candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 17:14-20. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD. Tewahedo dynastic witness: Kǝbrä Nägäśt.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On the king's Torah — 'when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book' (Deu 17:18-19) — Ephrem reads the king-as-Torah-scribe command as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of the doctrine that the king is FIRST a guardian of the law, only secondarily a ruler of the people. The king does not stand above the Torah; he copies it with his own hand and reads it all the days of his life. Tewahedo Solomonic-dynasty self-understanding, codified in the Kǝbrä Nägäśt (Glory of the Kings), cites Deu 17:18 as the canonical Old-Testament warrant for the Ethiopian-emperor-as-Torah-guardian — the emperor at coronation receives both crown and Tabot, and is sworn to defend both.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

On the king's Torah — 'when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, he shall write him a copy of this law in a book' (Deu 17:18-19) — Ephrem reads the king-as-Torah-scribe command as the canonical Old-Testament anchor of the doctrine that the king is FIRST a guardian of the law, only secondarily a ruler of the people. The king does not stand above the Torah; he copies it with his own hand and reads it all the days of his life. Tewahedo Solomonic-dynasty self-understanding, codified in the Kǝbrä Nägäśt (Glory of the Kings), cites Deu 17:18 as the canonical Old-Testament warrant for the Ethiopian-emperor-as-Torah-guardian — the emperor at coronation receives both crown and Tabot, and is sworn to defend both.
